description:
Found by the fz-kdt.107 cold review's Q4 dig (2026-09-01), on 00277's
180-vs-181 demand delta -- which is fz-kdt.106's transient class WITH A
BLOCKER, not a third class:

(1) LIFO mints Kernel.dbg/1[empty_list()] standing beside
Kernel.dbg/1[list(int)] -- ONE position, empty_list() <= list(int),
looks squarely absorbable by the landed dominance rule and is NOT
absorbed. Probe whether the rule is guarded away (free-var-set
inequality? lit-shape mismatch? the rows live in different FACTS --
dominance runs per-activation-fact inside insert_row, and dbg[empty] vs
dbg[list(int)] are different ACTIVATION KEYS, not rows of one key --
which would mean this hole is BY DESIGN of the row-level rule and the
cure lives at demand/key level instead). Diagnose before proposing.

(2) FIFO's Range.reduce/5[...{:cont,empty_list()}...] pair: two rows
differing only in the CAPTURED INNER CLOSURE (Enum.reverse/1#lambda vs
/2#lambda); the standing {:cont, list(:tail)} row would dominate the
payload but the closure position blocks dominance (lit_arrow_shapes
containment fails across distinct fn_ids) -- the same
shielding-by-callable-identity as fz-kdt.118's drop-rule blocker. If
118's observable-surface judgement is proven sound, the analogous
question arises here: should dominance compare closure positions
through their runtime-observable erasure? Same soundness obligation,
same review.
title: Two named holes in the kdt.106 absorption rule: a single-position dominated row survives, and closure positions shield domination
